title: Extending Programmable Blockchain Protocols to Enable and Incentivize Parallel Execution of Smart Contracts
venue: The 7th International Conference on Mathematical Research for Blockchain Economy
summary: Makes an execution schedule part of the block proposal and rewards producers for including transactions and using parallel hardware effectively.
abstract: The paper extends programmable blockchain protocols with explicit schedules for parallel transaction execution. Producers assign transactions to cores and time intervals subject to dependency constraints, and validators check the published schedule. A reward combining transaction fees and savings in completion time is calibrated to encourage parallelism without rewarding strategic transaction exclusion in the model. The schedule abstraction leaves finer-grained execution optimization for further work.
